requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The specification occupies one page and provides a readable entry for every shot, including source, selected WS/MS/CU size, action, dialogue or sound entry, character and timing. Archive records identify A01–A04 with the correct image, capture date, location, photographer and permission status from the register. Interview records correctly identify Ruth Cole and the credit requirement. Formatting may vary; missing fields, invented source facts or an incomplete six-shot plan fail.

Each document identifies S01–S06 in order and establishes intervals 0–3, 3–6, 6–9, 9–12, 12–13.5 and 13.5–15 seconds. Sources are respectively A01, A02, A03, A04, the present-day drawing and the title. Tables, diagrams or prose are acceptable if unambiguous; omitted shots, conflicting durations, reordered sources or a total other than 15 seconds fail.

The first page contains S01–S03 and the second S04–S06, with three sequential panels on each. Their combined source sequence and durations agree with the specification and fixed timeline. Every panel contains its annotation and subtitle placeholder; S01–S04 are archive panels, S05 is a drawing and S06 is the title. Panel arrangement may vary if reading order is clear. Missing, duplicated or misplaced shots, or placeholders supplied only outside the frames, fail.

Read all six panels and compare their metadata with both written sources. Each panel must show its S01–S06 ID, exactly one permitted shot-size code, the correct duration expressed in seconds and the prescribed character entry. The designer may choose any permitted size per shot, but that choice must agree across all three artifacts. Missing entries, alternative size vocabularies or mismatches fail.

Each study visibly presents its corresponding supplied photograph, an identifiable proposed crop, an explicit movement proposal and complete attribution. Collectively they cover A01–A04 once each. Source identity must remain recognizable: A01 has the open entrance and clear forecourt; A02 has bicycles on the left and tea trays on the right; A03 has closed doors and weeds; A04 has restored green doors and Ruth at the doorway. Crops may omit peripheral details, but the displayed source must be correct and treatment must not invent a different event. Crop and movement notation may vary.

Inspect every archive study and every S01–S04 image panel individually. Each must associate Archive and Bell Yard Hall, Bell Yard with the correct full date and prefixed photographer credit: A01—12 June 1938, Photograph by Arthur Bell; A02—8 September 1964, Photograph by Joan Mercer; A03—21 November 1991, Photograph by Peter Shaw; A04—14 April 2018, Photograph by Helen Cole. Line breaks and separators may vary. A page-level credit that leaves an individual storyboard frame uncredited, an abbreviated date or a swapped record fails.

The S05 panel and finished S05 image visibly carry Illustration as their source label. It must belong to the drawn frame rather than exist only as an external page note. Typography may vary within the required geometry; an absent label or an Archive label on S05 fails.

The character sheet supplies front, side and back views plus neutral, remembering and gently smiling expressions. Across the sheet and S05 depictions, Ruth remains recognizable from A04 through her short silver bob, round dark glasses and navy cardigan. Features need only be visible where the view permits; glasses need not be visible from behind. Illustration style and pose may vary, but missing required views or expressions, or replacement of an identifying feature, fail.

Compare visible architecture with the supplied photographs and plan. Preserve five evenly spaced upper windows, the central arched entrance and one circular gable vent wherever included. Maintain the red-brick facade and the dark green timber doors for 2018 and the present day. Archive perspectives must follow their registered north-facing viewpoints: A01 (21000, 14000), A02 (24000, 14000), A03 (36000, 14000), A04 (30000, 14000); S05 follows A04. Cropping, monochrome treatment and historically appropriate changes are allowed. Mirrored geography, invented facade features or a conflicting viewpoint fail.

Judge each shot frame within a storyboard page, and each standalone finished frame, against the supplied 16:9 geometry. Essential action respects a 3.5% inset and graphics a 5% inset. Attribution or illustration labels occupy x 5–95%, y 5–18%; subtitles or their placeholders occupy x 10–90%, y 78–93%; storyboard annotations occupy x 5–95%, y 68–74%; title text occupies x 10–90%, y 35–65%. Coordinates are measured from the frame's top left. Subtitles are bottom-centered and no more than two lines. Styling and background bleed may vary; displaced text zones or essential content outside its safe area fail.

The sheet covers S01–S06 and includes matching shot metadata and correct archive attribution records. It assigns T01 'My mother remembered the hall opening.' to 0–3 seconds, T02 'I carried the tea trays in 1964.' to 3–6, T03 'In 1991, we packed the chairs away.' to 6–9 and T04 'In 2018, we opened the doors again.' to 9–12, using identical words for interview audio and subtitles. It specifies bottom-centered subtitles of at most two lines, each lasting three seconds; Ruth Cole's on-screen speaker credit during S04; D01 'Ruth waits.' on the description track at 12–13.5; and ambient sound for the illustrated pause and title. Line wrapping may vary. Paraphrases, missing credits, shifted intervals or description placed over an interview excerpt fail.

S04 is a finished treatment of the A04 photograph, consistent with its study and storyboard, with Ruth at the doorway, her visible speaker name Ruth Cole and the exact T04 subtitle. The speaker name sits inside the graphics safe area between the upper label band and lower subtitle zone. S05 is a finished present-day drawing of Ruth waiting at the hall doorway from A04's viewpoint, using the daylight and material atmosphere supplied by bell-yard-today.png. Rendering style may vary. A rough placeholder, substituted photograph, reversed photographic/drawn roles or missing S04 speaker identification fails.

Both required strings must be visibly readable in the title composition with their specified spelling and case. Typeface, scale and line arrangement may vary within the prescribed title zone. Missing words, altered wording or text rendered too illegibly to establish the title fails.

Review the full playback and time its six shots: A01 at 0–3 seconds, A02 at 3–6, A03 at 6–9, A04 at 9–12, the present-day drawing at 12–13.5 and title at 13.5–15. The closing interval visibly carries BELL YARD VOICES and A street remembers and follows the delivered title design. Movement within shots may vary according to the approved studies. Additional or missing shots, changed source order, displaced boundaries or an incorrect closing title fail.

requirementChecks.criteria: During each archive shot, verify a readable Archive label, Bell Yard Hall, Bell Yard and its full date/credit pair: 12 June 1938 / Photograph by Arthur Bell; 8 September 1964 / Photograph by Joan Mercer; 21 November 1991 / Photograph by Peter Shaw; 14 April 2018 / Photograph by Helen Cole. Verify that Illustration remains visible throughout S05 and Ruth Cole is identified on screen during S04. Typographic arrangement may vary. Missing, swapped or unreadable records, or an illustration label absent for part of the drawn shot, fail.

requirementChecks.criteria: Listen to the full opening and inspect subtitles. S01–S04 must respectively speak and display 'My mother remembered the hall opening.', 'I carried the tea trays in 1964.', 'In 1991, we packed the chairs away.' and 'In 2018, we opened the doors again.' Subtitle intervals must be 0–3, 3–6, 6–9 and 9–12 seconds, each bottom-centered in no more than two lines. The description track delivers 'Ruth waits.' within 12–13.5 seconds, after the interview and before the title; S05 and S06 retain their ambient-sound roles. Line breaks and audio mixing may vary without changing words or timing. Paraphrases, missing audio or subtitles, wrong shot assignments or description overlapping the interview fail.

requirementChecks.criteria: Count at least eight pages and verify both exact title strings on the cover. The presentation explicitly links chronology, source attribution, S05's Illustration label, Ruth's silver bob/dark round glasses/navy cardigan and subtitle intervals to the relevant S01–S06 IDs. Archive dates and credits must match the register, and timing must match the fixed timeline. Page order and explanatory style may vary. A general mood presentation without shot-specific evidence, incorrect facts or a missing cover string fails.

Every listed source deliverable is visibly reused somewhere in the presentation. Resizing, readable excerpts and multi-item pages are allowed if each source is recognizable and its relevant content remains assessable. Merely mentioning a deliverable, substituting a different design or omitting any source fails.

Review the entire moving sequence in its 16:9 frame. Essential action stays within the 3.5% action inset and graphics within the 5% graphics inset. Source labels use x 5–95%, y 5–18%; subtitles use x 10–90%, y 78–93%; title wording uses x 10–90%, y 35–65%. Ruth's S04 speaker name remains between the label and subtitle bands inside graphics safety. Backgrounds may bleed to the edges. Camera movement or transitions that push required text or essential action outside its prescribed area fail.
